blockNote: Layer-1 scroll drivers (Bank 00, 59610-60053): three actor scripts that set the scroll position of the second background layer (cameraDeltaX / Y). Despite the block name they have nothing to do with sprites or visual effects.
=== SPAWN ===
- effect_position_update: scene actor record < X byte $01, Y byte $82 > in scene_actors entries $09 and $32 (scene_event_0C84BC, scene_event_0C9572).
- effect_velocity_init: record < $02, $02 > in scene_actors entries $4E and $50 (scene_event_0C9E92, scene_event_0CA01A).
- effect_subpixel_math: sg55_viper_arena (SpawnBeforeFlags #$2800, then $14 := $0201 and $16 := 0) and sg55_mystic_statue code_0ACE81 ($14 := $0201, $16 := $000C).
=== SPAWN BYTES = VELOCITY (the first two actors) ===

InitActorFromSceneData turns the record's X and Y bytes into pixels (byte x 16), so $14 >> 4 gives the X byte back and $16 >> 4 the Y byte. Both are decoded as sign-magnitude: bit 7 = negative, bits 0-6 = magnitude. The Y byte is decremented first, so Y byte 1 = 0, 2 = +1, $82 = -1; Y byte 0 gives $0081 (+129), a quirk the shipped records never use. Result: effect_position_update drifts at X +1, Y -1 px per frame; effect_velocity_init at X +2, Y +1.
=== VARIABLES ===

cameraTargetX / Y ($06BE / $06C2): layer-0 scroll target (camera_scroll_controller). cameraDeltaX / Y ($06C0 / $06C4): the layer-1 scroll POSITION, not a delta: CameraSmoothScroll (camera_tilemap) copies them to effectScrollH / V ($068C / $0690, the BG2 scroll) when layerPriorityFlag bit $0400 is set. effectDeltaX / Y ($06E4 / $06E6): written by camera_scroll_controller, how far the camera moved (target - current scroll); the drifters add it so layer 1 follows the camera. effectBoundsX / Y ($0694 / $0698): layer-1 width and height (set in scene_script). effectRenderDeltaX / Y ($06E8 / $06EA): written only by these actors; no reader was found outside scene_lifecycle, which clears them. forcedScrollOverride ($06C8): written here with bit 15 set, the same convention as ScrollCameraInit; no reader found (OQ-I051-2).

The old header said the actors seed and integrate velocities for 'cutscene camera takeover' and that effect_subpixel_math refines the other two every frame. The velocity decode and the integration are in the same actor, and effect_subpixel_math is independent: its $14 / $16 are a parallax ratio or a drift, not a subpixel remainder.

effect_velocity_init: Layer-1 drift at constant velocity, no bounds. Actor-def: sprite 0, flags 0, header byte $2C. The spawn bytes are decoded into $2C / $2E (see the block note), the offsets are zeroed, and after a one-frame wait the code integrates every frame: $14 / $16 are the accumulated layer-1 X / Y offset.

Per frame (after the WaitByte, apparently without an own SetEntryHere: OQ-I051-1): $14 += $2C + effectDeltaX and forcedScrollOverride := $14 | $8000 (X); $16 += $2E + effectDeltaY and cameraDeltaY := $16 (Y); effectRenderDeltaX := the X velocity ($2C), effectRenderDeltaY := cameraDeltaY - effectScrollV. The two axes are not symmetric: X never reaches cameraDeltaX.
partNotes.code_00E8DA: Init: $12 |= $1000 (display / overlay-active qualifier), decode the spawn X byte into $2C, then the Y byte (minus 1) into $2E, zero the offsets and the layer-1 scroll state, WaitByte 1, then the per-frame integration; the RTL ends each frame.

partNotes.loc_00E906: Y velocity stored in $2E; zero $14 / $16 and the layer-1 scroll state (effectScrollH / V, cameraDeltaX / Y).
effect_subpixel_math: Layer-1 parallax ratio or drift, run every frame. The spawner sets $14 (X) and $16 (Y). A word with a nonzero high byte is a RATIO lo / hi: the layer-1 position becomes the camera target x lo / hi (hardware_math.MulDivide: (A low x Y) / A high). $0201 = target x 1 / 2, so layer 1 scrolls at half speed (both sg55 spawns use it for X). With a zero high byte the signed low byte is ADDED every frame instead (for X bit 15 forces this mode too); sg55_mystic_statue sets $16 := $000C, +12 px per frame on cameraDeltaY.

The X result goes to forcedScrollOverride ($06C8, no reader found: OQ-I051-2), the Y result to cameraDeltaY. The X half returns through the PEA into EffectUpdateCameraDeltaY, whose RTL ends the frame.

Y: the same with $16, effectDeltaY and cameraDeltaY, except that a negative position wraps to effectBoundsY - 1 (X uses effectBoundsX itself, no -1).

blockNote: Post-boss stat catch-up actor (Bank 00, 49854-50070), spawned from scene_actors in the five boss arenas (Castoth, Viper, the Mu vampires, Sand Fanger, the Mummy Queen). Once the boss is dead it grants, in one go, the stat reward of every room of that dungeon whose clear reward the player has not yet taken.
=== FLOW ===

1. BossRewardCheckInit: find sceneCurrent in boss_reward_range_00C312 (4-byte rows: scene, first scene, last scene, pad; the first match wins). The row's byte offset is kept in $20, offset / 4 is the boss number. If wramFlags $0100 + boss number (event flags $0500-$0507) is already set the actor only idles.

2. Every frame (SetEntryHere): wait for playerFlags bit $0020 (boss defeated). Then BossClearApplyStatReward walks enemy_clear_reward_table over the scenes [first, last): each scene with a nonzero tier whose scene flag $0300 + scene is clear gets the flag set and its stat raised (1 = Max HP, 2 = STR, 3 = DEF, +1 each). It is the same flag that the per-room clear reward (reward_actors, field_reveal_object) tests, so a room cannot pay twice.
3. hpToHeal := maxHp - hp (UpdateHUD refills the bar at 1 HP per 8 frames, which also covers the extra max HP), the boss flag is set, and the actor idles for the rest of the scene.
=== QUIRKS ===

- The scene search has no end-of-table test; it relies on the actor existing only in the five boss arenas. Rows 5-10 are placeholders (scene $F8 and $29 with an empty range); the first $29 row is the real one.

- The range end is compared only after a zero tier. In the shipped table the entry at the end index (the boss scene itself) is zero in all five ranges, which ends the walk, so a nonzero run past the end cannot happen.
- The entry stores the range word in the actor's $04 and the apply routine uses $04 and $0E as scratch. wram-memory-map lists $04 as prevActorLink (the actor list predecessor): OQ-I051-3.
- The old header called the HP effect a 'damage-flash timer'; $0B22 is the heal counter hpToHeal. The old routine comment said the flags are per enemy; the index is the scene id.

blockNote: Gem / stat-item pickup spawned by the field-reveal events (Bank 00, 55928-56200): it drops to the floor, hops once, becomes a pullable pickup (collect_handler_gem child) and, if it is a gem, expires.
=== SPAWN ===

SpawnAfterFlags ( field_reveal_object, #$0020 ) from EnemyDefeatDispatch (every kill but the last; the child's $26 = enemies remaining, nonzero), pyCC_mystic_ball (771837) and awB1_wall_walker (769369) (child $26 = 0). The spawn copies the spawner's position and statsPtr ($7F0020).
=== WHICH PICKUP ===

- $26 nonzero, or the room's clear reward already taken (TestFlag_0300(sceneCurrent) set), or tier 0: FieldRevealFromActorStats reads the byte at +3 of the spawner's stat table. & 3 = 0 dies at once; 1 / 2 / 3 = a gem pickup with anim $04 / $05 / $06 and item $83 / $84 / $85 (1 / 2 / 5 gems, given by GiveItemToPlayer).

- Otherwise enemy_clear_reward_table[sceneCurrent] & 3 picks the room's stat item: 1 / 2 / 3 = anim $0C / $0D / $0E (the sprites of e_hp / e_str / e_def_increase) and item $80 / $81 / $82 (Max HP / STR / DEF + 1). These paths also store $FFFF in orbitAngle (no reader found: OQ-I051-4). Nothing here sets scene flag $0300 (reward_actors does for the last-kill reward): OQ-I051-5.
=== DROP AND LIFE ===

loc_00DB0B stores the item id in chatPtr ($7F000A), remembers the spawn Y in $24 and sets $26 := 7 (the step budget). With Y aligned to a 16 px row it probes the tile with BranchIfSolidHere: while the tile is solid it moves one row (16 px) down, at most 8 rows, and stops early on a tile whose collision byte is $0E; after 8 failures the target is the spawn Y + 1. The target goes to moveXAlt / moveYAlt, the actor returns to its spawn Y, flies to the target (MoveToward, 4 px per frame), hops once (Y chain $45: -2, -2, -1, -1, 0, 0, +1, +1, +2, +2), waits 11 frames and spawns collect_handler_gem (SpawnAfterMarked #$2300): holding L / R then pulls the pickup toward the player.

It then animates in 100-frame blocks. A stat item (anim $0C-$0E, at least 8) repeats forever. A gem (anim $04-$06) switches to anim + 5 after the first block (the blink animations $09 / $0A / $0B, inferred: OQ-I051-7), plays 10 more frames and falls into FieldRevealDieEmpty (Die): a gem lives about 110 frames.

The old header said it checks that all enemies are cleared and stages HP / STR / DEF gem sprites. The flag means 'this room's reward is already taken', and only the tier path stages stat items; the gem path stages gems.

blockNote: Enemy defeat dispatcher with a kill counter (Bank 0A, 697407-697568). A trimmed variant of StandardEnemyDefeatHandler used as a death callback by three enemies: gw82_fire_bug (SetDeathCallback code_0B8DB9), av6D_dive_bat (code_0AEF2E) and gw8A_sand_fanger (JumpFar), each reaching it with COP JumpFar. $0AEC is the number of enemies left on the map (hex) and $0AEE the same count in BCD (ram_map.txt).
=== FLOW ===

- $0AEC = 1 (this is the last enemy): clear the ForceDir bits ($6000 of $12), halt movement (StageMoveXY #0, #0 selects the zero chain; moveScratch1 / 2 = $7F002C / $7F002E cleared) and JumpFar into StandardEnemyDefeatHandler, which decrements the counters itself, plays the full defeat and gives the clear reward (EnemyStatBonusReward when the remaining count reaches 0).

- Otherwise: CallNear EnemyDefeatDispatch_CountKill (below), then SpawnAfterFlags ( @field_reveal_object, #$0020 ), store the remaining count (orbitAngle, saved by the subroutine) in the child's $26 and Die. field_reveal_object treats a nonzero $26 as 'use this enemy's own stats': FieldRevealFromActorStats reads the low two bits of the stat-table byte at +3 of the defeated enemy: 0 = nothing, 1 / 2 / 3 = a gem pickup worth 1 / 2 / 5 gems (item $83 / $84 / $85). So every kill but the last can drop its own gem. The HP / STR / DEF items of field_reveal_object come only from its room-reward tier path, which this caller does not use (the old note said 'Spawn stat gem reveal', and an earlier version of this note called the byte a HP / STR / DEF gem).

EnemyDefeatDispatch_CountKill (a CallNear subroutine, returns with RestoreSavedPtr): death sound #03 (the standard handler uses #06), BCD decrement of $0AEE, hex decrement of $0AEC stored also in orbitAngle ($7F0010,X) for the spawned actors, halt movement, spawn EnemyDeathFlash (flags $0302), SetDungeonKillFlag (the actor's enemyNum bit in the wramFlags bitfield), $10 |= $2000 (script-driven run path), ClearSolidHere when extendedFlags bit $0008 is set, and the field-reveal bookkeeping: when deathActionIdx ($7F0024) is nonzero and event flag $0100 + idx is not yet set (TestFlag_0100 carry clear), set it and spawn SpawnFieldRevealEffect (flags $0342) with the index copied into the child's deathActionIdx.

Differences from StandardEnemyDefeatHandler: no boss / stat-table checks (the three callers are ordinary enemies), no WaitByte, no EnemyGemDropRouter call (a field_reveal_object child is spawned instead; it reads the same stat-table byte at +3), and the $12 |= $1000 priority boost on the flash is not applied. The old header said it 'decrements ... plays death SFX, spawns death flash, sets dungeon kill flag, optionally clears collision tile' which is right; it did not explain the field_reveal_object spawn or the callers.
Edge case: the test is for exactly 1. If $0AEC were 0 the counters would wrap to $FFFF / $99 (BCD) and $26 would be nonzero (OQ-I046-4). UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME.

blockNote: Camera drift library (Bank 00, 53134-53350): three short-lived actor scripts that nudge the camera during set pieces. Scene scripts spawn them with SpawnAfterFlags / SpawnListAppend; each dies when finished.
=== CALLERS ===

CameraDriftLoopSimple: pyCD_flame_statue, ir25_ceiling_tile, ir29_castoth. CameraDriftLoopShip: st68_kara (Angel Village undersea tunnel), gs2D_lily, gs2D_lance, gs2B_erik (Gold Ship). CameraDriftPatterned: awB1_gorgon, pyD9_dangerslide_controller, ir29_castoth (3 sites).
=== VARIABLES ===

cameraTargetX / Y ($06BE / $06C2) are the layer-0 scroll targets (camera_scroll_controller recomputes them each frame). cameraDeltaX / Y ($06C0 / $06C4) are the layer-1 (second background layer) scroll POSITION, not per-frame deltas: the visual_effect_pipeline actors and camera_scroll write them, and CameraSmoothScroll copies them to effectScrollH / V ($068C / $0690, the BG2 scroll) when layerPriorityFlag bit $0400 is set. While that mode is active the drift therefore moves both layers together. These are not the effectDeltaX / Y ($06E4 / $06E6) that camera_scroll_controller writes. Whether the offsets added here survive the recompute is not established statically (OQ-I050-2).
=== CameraDriftLoopSimple ===

LoopStart #$78 runs 120 passes, one frame each (every LoopEnd pass yields). Each pass adds r = (RngByte and 3) - 1, that is -1, 0, +1 or +2 (bias +0.5), to cameraTargetY and to cameraDeltaY. Nothing is undone at the end. The same formula is the Y shake in player_character. Then Die. The old note said 'random +-1'.
=== CameraDriftLoopShip ===

Sets $12 bit $1000 (the display / overlay-active qualifier, so the drift also runs in the display-filtered modes) and $26 := 0 ($26 = the offset applied last frame). 120 passes: while playerFlags bit $0100 (forced walk) is set a pass does nothing; otherwise cameraDeltaY -= $26 (undo last frame), $26 := RngByte and 3 (0 to 3), then cameraTargetY += $26 and cameraDeltaY += $26. After the loop it yields once (SetEntryHereAndYield), subtracts the last $26 from cameraDeltaY and dies. So the delta offset is temporary (each frame replaces the previous one) while the target offset is not undone here.
=== CameraDriftPatterned ===

$28 := RngByte (random starting phase), $2A := 2, SetEntryHere. Each run: DBR := program bank (to read camera_drift_offsets), Y offset := table[$28 and 7] then $28++, added to cameraTargetY (a negative result is clamped to 0) and, unless $24 = $FFFF, to cameraDeltaY (clamped to 0); then the X offset := table[$28 and 7], i.e. the next entry, with the same rules. A run is followed by $08 := 3 (3 frames) and DEC $2A; the third run ends in Die, so the actor lives about 9 frames and applies 3 Y and 3 X offsets. The next run's Y entry is the previous run's X entry.

camera_drift_offsets holds 16 words but the index is masked to 3 bits, so only the first 8 are used: +1, -1, -2, +1, +2, 0, -2, +1 (sum 0). The last 8 words (+5, -4, -2, +4, +1, -5, +4, -3, also summing to 0) are never read.
